title: Warren Buffett at Fortune MPW 2014: good businesses, zone of reasonableness, ignoring macro noise
summary: Buffett explains what makes a good business (high return on tangible assets, bought at a sensible price), why banks lose money copying competitors, and why the market sits in a "zone of reasonableness." He also covers owning stocks without anchoring to cost, admitting mistakes early, and ignoring politics and macro forecasts.

principles.text: A good business earns a high return on tangible assets; overpaying can turn it into a bad investment.
principles.quote: a good business is the one that earns a high rate of return on on tangible assets very simple

principles.text: Buying a bad business at a cheap price was an early mistake; it took decades to learn.
principles.quote: the big mistake which we made in the early years was to try and buy a bad business at a really cheap price and uh it took me about 20 or 30 years to figure out that wasn't a good idea

principles.text: Don't copy competitors; if the reason is that others are doing it, go back to square one.
principles.quote: if anybody comes to me and says we want to do this because the other guy is doing it you know I say go back to square one and come up with a better reason

principles.text: Markets sit in a broad zone of reasonableness; precise timing is impossible and unnecessary.
principles.quote: if you if you buy good businesses at reasonable prices and hold them you're going to make a lot of money

principles.text: A stock doesn't know what you paid; the only question is whether you can get more for your money elsewhere.
principles.quote: the stock doesn't even care that you own it you are nothing to the stock that's that stock is everything to you

principles.text: Don't let politics, Fed moves or macro forecasts change decisions on businesses meant to be held for decades.
principles.quote: the important thing is whether we get a good business with good management at a sensible price
